label: Boerhaave
summary: Dutch physician, botanist and chemist (1668–1738), professor at Leiden and the most influential clinical teacher of his century.

label: white poppy (papaver album)
summary: The opium poppy; 'papaver album' of the old pharmacy is its white-seeded form, whose bruised seeds were the classic basis of soothing emulsions.

label: diacodium (poppy-head syrup)
summary: Syrupus diacodii, a mild opiate syrup boiled from dried poppy capsules; a standard pediatric and night-time anodyne of the period.
canonical: Papaver somniferum L. (preparation: Syrupus diacodii, syrup of poppy heads)

label: opium (tinctura opii)
summary: Dried latex of the opium poppy; here as a tincture in rectified spirit of wine — essentially laudanum — dosed by drops.
canonical: opium (dried latex of Papaver somniferum L.)

label: barley (hordeum)
summary: Barley; 'aqua decocti hordei' (barley water) was the standard demulcent vehicle for drawing up emulsions.

label: cinnamon (cinnamomum)
summary: Cinnamon bark, used here as distilled cinnamon water — an aromatic cordial flavouring the narcotic emulsion.

label: citron peel (cortex citrei)
summary: Peel of the citron, an aromatic bitter; the recipe adds its distilled water to flavour and 'corroborate' the emulsion.

label: milk thistle (carduus Mariae)
summary: Our Lady's thistle or milk thistle; its seeds head the list of the lubricating, diuretic emulsion.

label: burdock (bardana)
summary: Burdock; its seeds, ground into the emulsion, were a stock diuretic of the old materia medica.

label: fennel (foeniculum)
summary: Fennel: seed in the diuretic emulsion and distilled fennel water in the worm emulsion — carminative and a traditional vermifuge vehicle.

label: sweet almond (amygdala dulcis)
summary: Sweet almonds, twenty in number — the classic emulsive kernel that gives these milky mixtures their body.

label: liquorice root (radix liquiritiae)
summary: Liquorice root; its sweet infusion is the liquid in which the seeds of recipe 6 are drawn up into an emulsion.

label: sal prunella (mineral drug)
summary: Not a plant: fused and purified nitre cast into balls, a favourite 'cooling' diuretic salt of the period.

label: opopanax (gummi opoponacis)
summary: A fetid gum-resin from the roots of a Mediterranean umbellifer, prescribed here as the active of the worm-expelling emulsion.

label: Venice soap (sapo venetus)
summary: Fine white Castile-type soap of olive oil and soda, used internally as a detergent, laxative and (as here) anthelmintic adjuvant.
canonical: Venice soap — hard white olive-oil and soda soap (a manufactured preparation, no taxon)

label: mugwort (artemisia)
summary: Syrup of artemisia — officinally syrup of mugwort — sweetens the worm emulsion with a herb itself reputed anthelmintic.

label: Boerhaave, Libellus de materia medica ('Mat. Med.')

mentions.quote: Boerhaave, the same work [Materia Medica], p. 229.

summary: Boerhaave's formulary companion to his Aphorisms — the work all three 'V. Boerh. Mat. Med.' page references on this page point into.
canonical: Herman Boerhaave, Libellus de materia medica et remediorum formulis, quae serviunt Aphorismis de cognoscendis et curandis morbis (Leiden: Isaac Severinus, 1719, and later editions) — the 'Boerh. Mat. Med.' of the citation formula
